BUILDPLAN.md T-02 (M0).

`web/shared/`: tokens and fonts vendored from the design system; port `proto.js` — source well, syntax colour, trace renderer, the type model with measured refit and the clipped-edge, the phase strings from `SPEC.md` §11

Criteria: AC-99, AC-100, AC-40
Harness hooks: see EVALUATION.md rows for those IDs; `just test` is the inner loop (≤ 60 s).
Depends on (BUILDPLAN): T-01
BUILDPLAN notes: Built alone; three tickets consume it

Orchestrator notes: Put the ported §11 phase strings in `web/shared/copy` from the start so T-22 moves nothing (F-11). Port from `prototypes/_shared/proto.js`, `tokens.css`; fonts from the design system per SPEC §15 (D-14). The source well font size is behaviour (SPEC §5.2), never read off the prototype; every other size is the prototype's.

Workflow mode: inline-full. Terminal pre-merge status: review. PR base: origin/main.
Standing clauses: criteria outrank SPEC on behaviour, state, payloads and copy; SPEC outranks the prototype, which wins on visual detail only. Never write down what a program prints. Answer position is a uniform draw from the date, never balanced. Miri proves absence of UB on executed paths only. Colour is never the only signal. Code never causes horizontal page scroll. Never `git add -A`. Signing goes through 1Password: retry once, then escalate.

Plan: filled in by the delegator's plan phase.
data.title: Shared web layer: tokens, fonts, well, type model

data.body: READY PQ-2 CWD /Users/michellerojas/rust-nyc-pop-quiz-worktrees/shared-web-layer HEAD 2ab95e31b78ee48a7067dc47904e98b28baf3d37 BASE 2ab95e31b78ee48a7067dc47904e98b28baf3d37 MODE active

ORCHESTRATOR RULING: where the ticket text and your boot brief differ, the brief governs (it is later and knows about PR #8). PR base is ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold until #8 merges; fly, push and PR commands run in your tab with the client's approval. The worktree .claude/settings.json now also allows sandboxed writes to /Users/michellerojas/rust-nyc-pop-quiz/.lattice, so lattice commands should no longer need the bypass; git fetch/push over SSH still do.

ORCHESTRATOR: PR #8 merged to main at 0742d35 (merge commit; your base commit 2ab95e3 is its second parent). From now on: rebase onto origin/main (git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main; it should be a no-op or trivial), and open your PR against main, not ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold. Drop the 'Based on #8' line from the PR body.

CONTRACT DEFECTS from PQ-2 planning — reported, not fixed (ground rule 7).

1. SPEC.md §15 is wrong about Instrument Serif. It says both Cascadia Mono and Instrument Serif 'ship in web/shared/fonts/ from the design system's assets/fonts/' (D-14). The design system (claude.ai/artifact/2k3zt9WWz6XUZRjkLDWvfi, 123 files) carries Cascadia Mono — project/fonts/CascadiaMono-VariableFont_wght.ttf and -Italic-, plus project/assets/fonts/OFL.txt — and carries NO Instrument Serif file at all. --font-heading names the family but the prototype got the face from the Google Fonts CDN @import that D-14 forbids. PQ-2 takes Cascadia Mono from the design system (§15 honoured exactly, no network) and Instrument Serif from its upstream OFL release per the boot prompt, checksummed. §15 needs amending.

2. prototypes/_shared/tokens.css §1 line 22 is a Google Fonts CDN @import, inside the block the ticket calls 'verbatim'. Irreconcilable with D-14, AC-77 (segment runs with outbound network blocked) and AC-102 (static file makes zero network requests). PQ-2 drops that one line and imports the vendored fonts.css instead; everything else in §1 is byte-identical.

3. web/README.md:25 documents the web suite as 'node --test web/test/'. On Node 22 that resolves the directory as a CommonJS module path and fails with Cannot find module .../web/test before any test runs. justfile:46 is correct ('node --test web/test/*.test.js') so just test is green — only the doc is wrong. web/README.md is not in PQ-2's cleared file list.

4. Naming drift for T-05/T-12: prototypes/_shared/data.js calls the third explanation beat 'argue' (proto.js explainHtml reads e.argue). SPEC.md §3.1 names it 'takeaway'. 'argue' also contains the substring 'argu', which SPEC §11's Forbidden row matches case-insensitively — harmless as a field name, a trap if it ever reaches a participant-facing string or a naive lint. The consuming tickets should use 'takeaway'.

Also: every token value in tokens.css §1 was compared against the design system's own project/tokens.css and matches exactly (colour ramps, spacing, type scale, radius, shadow, both font stacks). §1's verbatim claim holds.

ORCHESTRATOR RULINGS on your four findings. (1) Approved as planned: Cascadia Mono from the design system, Instrument Serif from its upstream OFL release with checksum and licence; routed upstream as F-16 (SPEC §15's provenance claim is wrong). (2) Approved: drop the Google Fonts @import line and import the vendored fonts.css; the prototype is patched where it violates a criterion, never copied — routed as F-17. (3) You are cleared to fix web/README.md line 25 to match the justfile; one line, say so in the completion comment. (4) Recorded for T-05 and T-12's briefs: the field is 'takeaway' per SPEC §3.1, never 'argue'. Proceed.

BASE CHANGE — PR #8 merged during PQ-2 planning. origin/ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold was deleted on merge and my fetch pruned it, so the boot prompt's base ref no longer resolves. main moved 7abfce0 -> 0742d35 (merge commit 'Merge pull request #8 from mrojas54/ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold'); 2ab95e3 is now an ancestor of origin/main and main carries the scaffold's justfile and web/ tree.

Per the boot prompt ('the Orchestrator retargets your PR to main once #8 merges') I have taken the retarget myself rather than stall: rebased onto origin/main (fast-forward, no conflicts, 0 commits of mine at the time), and the PR will open against main directly. The 'Based on #8 — merge that first; this PR retargets to main afterwards.' line is dropped from the PR body because it would now be false. Say so if you wanted that line kept or the stack preserved.

BLOCKED on commit signing — needs_human.

Commit 123cbc7 (fonts + stylesheets) signed fine at 18:20. Every commit since fails:
  error: 1Password: failed to fill whole buffer
  fatal: failed to write commit object
Three attempts (two backgrounded, one foreground). Per ground rule 5 I have not disabled or bypassed signing and have not committed unsigned.

Diagnosis: the 1Password SSH AGENT is healthy and unlocked — ssh-add -l over the agent socket lists four keys including SHA256:ZmDAi3no4K32bND+82CGabBv2D2VGJ7CsBZHH1MV5c4, the same key that signed 123cbc7. So the vault is not locked. The failure is in op-ssh-sign, the git signing helper, which is a separate IPC path to the desktop app and appears to be waiting on an approval prompt that a non-TTY tool call cannot answer.

NOTHING IS LOST. All work is on disk and staged. The remaining two commits are ready to go the moment signing works.

State: origin/main 0742d35 -> 123cbc7 (fonts, stylesheets) committed and signed. Staged and uncommitted: web/shared/{dom,phase,well,trace,typemodel,copy,check}.js, web/shared/README.md, web/test/{_load,phase,well,trace,typemodel,copy,check}*.js.

Tests are green: just test-web is 97/97 in 0.31-0.36s warm; just test-room passes in 0.27-0.48s.

SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT, not mine and not blocking me: just test cannot pass on this machine at all. test-pipeline dies with SIGABRT because the pyenv Python 3.12.10 cannot start — dyld: Library not loaded /usr/local/opt/gettext/lib/libintl.8.dylib (an Intel-path Homebrew dylib on an Apple Silicon box). Reproduced identically in a throwaway worktree at origin/main, so it predates this branch and affects every delegator that runs just test locally. Also, inside the session sandbox test-pipeline fails earlier still, on uv being unable to write ~/.cache/uv.

Remedy for signing I can take once a human says so: either approve the 1Password prompt and I retry as-is, or switch gpg.ssh.program to ssh-keygen so signing goes through the already-working agent socket with the SAME key — still a real signature, but it edits git config, so I will not do it unasked.

UNBLOCKED. Client approved signing through ssh-keygen. Passed per-invocation as 'git -c gpg.ssh.program=ssh-keygen' rather than written into git config, so nothing persists into the other worktrees; SSH_AUTH_SOCK points at the 1Password agent, which was healthy all along. Same key as before — SHA256:ZmDAi3no4K32bND+82CGabBv2D2VGJ7CsBZHH1MV5c4.

Three commits, all verifying G: 123cbc7 fonts+stylesheets, 4c6e55e the modules, b498ad8 the tests and README. Moving to code review.

DONE PQ-2 PR https://github.com/mrojas54/rust-nyc-pop-quiz/pull/9 HEAD 223a2018c1571bc913ec04e7915c7c6649f5fc41 BASE 0742d3578726e3e0486c7b3793c6bb934e3e8579 test-warm 0.44-0.64s (just test-web; see deviation 11) CI green 1/1 on the PR head

Five signed commits, 25 files, all inside web/shared/** and web/test/**. 103 tests. Code review PASS-WITH-NITS after three rounds. Browser validation 34/34.

deviations:
1. tokens.css §1 is verbatim but for one line: its Google Fonts @import, which D-14 forbids and AC-77/AC-102 would have caught later. Replaced by an import of the vendored fonts.css. Every other value compared against the design system's own generated token file and matching.
2. components.css added, which the deliverable list did not name. The well, trace, syntax-colour and provenance CSS live outside §1 of the prototype stylesheet, and a 'ported source well' that ships no well styling is not the well. Nothing restyled; each block names its source section and lines.
3. phase.js added, also not in the list. AC-99 is three-valued — colour on, colour off, no source — and one boolean cannot express it. Both predicates throw on an unknown phase rather than defaulting to colour on.
4. No rounding inside the refit loop. The prototype rounded to one decimal twice per pass; SPEC §5.2 rounds nowhere. T-19 mirrors this arithmetic and intermediate rounding is how two implementations come to disagree.
5. SPEC's screen_height_ft as its own configured value and READ_RATIO as a constant, over the prototype's width-derived height and live ratio control. Both give a 14.2px floor to one decimal.
6. The prototype's split-column code areas (564x426) are not ported at all. 'split' in SPEC is a PHASE taking the reading layout; in the prototype it was the side-by-side layout the client rejected at T-20 item 15.
7. Instrument Serif comes from its upstream OFL release, not the design system — see the contract defect below.
8. check.js's API changed during review: correctParts is gone and CORRECT_CLASS is not exported. Anything that could obtain the bare class could apply it without the glyph. This was a fix to the code after two failed attempts to fix it in the test.
9. escapeAttr added beyond a pure port. escapeHtml is safe for text but not inside a quoted attribute, and the consuming tickets may pass a bank-derived aria-label.
10. PR base is main, not ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold. PR #8 merged mid-ticket and the branch was deleted; I took the retarget the boot prompt anticipated. The 'Based on #8' line is omitted from the PR body because it would be false.
11. just test cannot complete on this machine — see notes. I report just test-web's warm time instead and treat CI as the real check.
12. copy.test.js runs the §11 Forbidden patterns and the §11.1 trope patterns over its own strings, with EVALUATION.md's retired-strings fixture. T-22 still owns the reusable lint and AC-42's row; this only proves my own transcription is clean and that my pattern copies actually fire.

notes:
- FOUR CONTRACT DEFECTS were reported in an earlier comment and none is fixed here: SPEC §15 is wrong that Instrument Serif ships from the design system (it is not there at all — Cascadia Mono is); tokens.css §1 contains a font CDN import; web/README.md:25 documents a node --test invocation that fails on Node 22 while the justfile is correct; and prototypes/_shared/data.js names the third explanation beat 'argue' where SPEC §3.1 says 'takeaway', which also happens to contain the Forbidden substring 'argu'.
- FOR T-19: mirror floorPx, sourceMetrics and desiredFontPx, share TYPE_CONSTANTS and CODE_AREA, and test against the same eight §5.2 worked examples. web/shared/README.md says so.
- FOR T-05/T-06/T-12 AND THE REVIEW TICKET: AC-40 is NOT discharged. EVALUATION.md names four surfaces and this ticket proves only the shared helper; each surface carries its own assertion.
- FOR T-05: transform: scale() does not reduce an element's layout width, so the 1120px canvas still claims 1120px of the page at scale(0.62). Found while validating. The projector page will scroll sideways unless the scaled canvas is clipped by a wrapper.
- KNOWN AC-40 GAP, disclosed in check.js's header and in the tests: a two-condition AND-gate inside openTag or applyCorrect evades the Proxy sweep, because JS short-circuits before the second key is ever read. The reviewer built one independently to confirm the disclaimer was honest. Not a live defect; closing it would need combinatorial key sweeps.
- ENVIRONMENT, affects every delegator: just test aborts with SIGABRT because the pyenv Python 3.12.10 cannot start — dyld: Library not loaded /usr/local/opt/gettext/lib/libintl.8.dylib, an Intel-path Homebrew dylib on an Apple Silicon box. Reproduced at origin/main in a throwaway worktree, so it predates this branch. Inside the session sandbox it fails earlier still, on uv writing ~/.cache/uv.
- SIGNING: op-ssh-sign failed repeatedly with 'failed to fill whole buffer' while the 1Password SSH agent was healthy and held the key. I escalated to needs_human rather than bypass; the client approved signing through ssh-keygen, passed per-invocation as git -c gpg.ssh.program=ssh-keygen so nothing persists into other worktrees. All five commits verify G with the same key as before.
